n: Alvar Aalto's architectural style is Modernism (Humanist/Organic Modernism). Alvar Aalto is known for a humanistic, organic strand of Modernism that integrates natural materials and forms.

q: Which German architect, a pioneer of Expressionist architecture who also contributed to the development of the International Style, designed the Einstein Tower in Potsdam using no historical precedents?
n: A German architect and a pioneer of Expressionist architecture who also contributed to the development of the International Style, using no historical precedents in his designs. Notable works: the Einstein Tower in Potsdam, Germany, and the Mossehaus in Berlin.

q: Which Swiss-French architect and urban planner, a pioneer of modern functional design who believed in the possibilities of mass production for domestic living, designed the Villa Savoye and the Unité d'Habitation?
n: A Swiss-French architect and urban planner, a pioneer of modern functional architecture known for his belief in the possibilities of mass production applied to domestic living. Notable works: Villa Savoye (France), Unité d'Habitation (Marseille), Notre-Dame du Haut (Ronchamp), and his urban plan for Chandigarh, India.

q: What is Eliel Saarinen's architectural style?
n: Eliel Saarinen's architectural style is Art Nouveau / Nordic Romanticism (early), Modernism (later). Eliel Saarinen began in Art Nouveau/National Romanticism before influencing American Modernist design.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Louvre Pyramid (1989); and Bank of China Tower (1990). Who is this architect?
n: I.M. Pei's notable works are the Louvre Pyramid (1989) in Paris and the Bank of China Tower (1990) in Hong Kong, characterized by its sharp angles and triangular frameworks.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Banqueting House (1619), Whitehall, London. Who is this architect?
n: Inigo Jones's notable work is the Banqueting House (1619) in Whitehall, London — the first building in England designed in a pure classical style.

q: What is Santiago Calatrava's architectural style?
n: Santiago Calatrava's architectural style is Structural Expressionism / Neo-Futurism. Santiago Calatrava is known for sculptural, dynamic structures inspired by natural forms — Structural Expressionism.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Robie House (1910); Fallingwater (1935); Taliesin West (1937); and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum (1959). Who is this architect?
n: Frank Lloyd Wright's notable works are the Robie House (1910) at the University of Chicago campus, Fallingwater (1935), Taliesin West (1937) in Scottsdale, Arizona, and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum (1959) in New York City.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Villa Savoye, France; Unité d'Habitation, Marseille; Notre-Dame du Haut, Ronchamp; and Chandigarh, India (urban planning and buildings). Who is this architect?
n: Le Corbusier's notable works are Villa Savoye in France, Unité d'Habitation in Marseille, Notre-Dame du Haut in Ronchamp, and the urban planning and buildings of Chandigarh, India.

q: What is Inigo Jones's architectural style?
n: Inigo Jones's architectural style is Classical Architecture (Palladianism). Inigo Jones introduced pure classical, Palladian-influenced architecture to Britain.

q: What is Pier Luigi Nervi's architectural style?
n: Pier Luigi Nervi's architectural style is Structural Engineering / Modernism. Pier Luigi Nervi combined engineering precision with architectural elegance in reinforced concrete.

q: Which American architect and designer, a prominent figure of the postmodernist movement known for integrating classical elements with whimsy and color — and for designing a famous Alessi teakettle — created the Portland Building in Oregon?
n: An American architect and designer, a prominent figure in the postmodernist movement, known for integrating classical elements into modern design with a sense of whimsy and color, including the iconic Alessi teakettle. Notable work: the Portland Building, Oregon, a landmark of postmodern architecture.

q: Which English-born American architect, often called the 'father of American architecture,' introduced Greek Revival architecture to the United States and contributed to the design of the U.S. Capitol?
n: An English-born American architect, often referred to as the 'father of American architecture.' He introduced Greek Revival architecture to the United States. Notable works: the Bank of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia and contributions to the design of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.

q: What is Fumihiko Maki's architectural style?
n: Fumihiko Maki's architectural style is Metabolism / Modernism. Fumihiko Maki, a founding Metabolist, is known for refined modernist designs blending Japanese and Western sensibility.

q: What is Geoffrey Bawa's architectural style?
n: Geoffrey Bawa's architectural style is Tropical Modernism. Geoffrey Bawa is revered as the 'Father of Tropical Modernism,' adapting Modernist principles to tropical climates.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Heritance Kandalama Hotel, Dambulla, Sri Lanka. Who is this architect?
n: Geoffrey Bawa's notable work is the Heritance Kandalama Hotel, Dambulla, Sri Lanka — considered one of his greatest masterpieces and an early pioneer of sustainable, eco-integrated hospitality design.

q: Which Canadian American architect, known for a deconstructivist style of unconventional, sculptural forms, used aerospace design software to help create the titanium-clad Guggenheim Museum Bilbao — crediting a phenomenon later dubbed the 'Bilbao Effect' — and the Walt Disney Concert Hall?
n: A Canadian American architect known for a deconstructivist style characterized by unconventional forms and innovative use of materials, often using aerospace design software to realize his sculptural designs. Notable works: the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao (1997), credited with revitalizing the city (the 'Bilbao Effect'), and the Walt Disney Concert Hall (2003) in Los Angeles.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: AEG Turbine Factory, Berlin; Mannesmann Building, Düsseldorf; and German Embassy, St. Petersburg. Who is this architect?
n: Peter Behrens's notable works are the AEG Turbine Factory in Berlin, a landmark of industrial architecture, the Mannesmann Building in Düsseldorf, and the German Embassy in St. Petersburg.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Red House, Bexleyheath; Standen House, West Sussex; and 1 Palace Green, London. Who is this architect?
n: Philip Webb's notable works are the Red House in Bexleyheath, designed for William Morris as a seminal Arts and Crafts residence, Standen House in West Sussex, and 1 Palace Green in London.

q: What is Marcel Breuer's architectural style?
n: Marcel Breuer's architectural style is Brutalism (Bauhaus origins). Marcel Breuer, a Bauhaus protégé, popularized exposed 'béton brut' concrete central to Brutalism.

q: Which Iraqi-British architect, who in 2004 became the first woman to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize, pioneered Parametricism alongside her partner Patrik Schumacher and designed the fluid, curvaceous Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku, earning the nickname 'Queen of the Curve'?
n: An Iraqi British architect who fundamentally redefined the possibilities of form and space in the 21st century. Alongside her partner Patrik Schumacher, she pioneered Parametricism, and in 2004 became the first woman to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize. Nicknamed the 'Queen of the Curve.' Notable works: the Heydar Aliyev Center (Baku), the Vitra Fire Station (Germany), and the MAXXI Museum (Rome).

q: What is Victor Horta's architectural style?
n: Victor Horta's architectural style is Art Nouveau. Victor Horta was a pioneer of the Art Nouveau movement, integrating architecture with decorative ironwork.

q: What is Robert Venturi's architectural style?
n: Robert Venturi's architectural style is Postmodernism. Robert Venturi was a leading theorist of Postmodernism, advocating 'complexity and contradiction.'

q: Which Italian architect and theorist, author of L'Architettura della città (The Architecture of the City) and designer of the San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena, championed the concept of 'Collective Memory' — the idea that urban form preserves the history and identity of its citizens?
n: An influential Italian architect and theorist, celebrated for his work in architectural theory and urban design. His seminal book, L'Architettura della città, emphasizes historical continuity in urban planning. Notable work: the San Cataldo Cemetery, Modena, Italy. He is closely associated with the concept of 'Collective Memory.'

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Cathedral of Brasília, Brazil; National Congress of Brazil; Palácio da Alvorada (Presidential Palace), Brasília; and Museum of Contemporary Art, Niterói. Who is this architect?
n: Oscar Niemeyer's notable works are the Cathedral of Brasília, the National Congress of Brazil, the Palácio da Alvorada (Presidential Palace) in Brasília, and the Museum of Contemporary Art in Niterói.

q: Which Dutch architect and theorist, founder of the Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA), is known for unconventional designs and influential urbanist writings, including the CCTV Headquarters in Beijing and the Seattle Central Library?
n: A Dutch architect and theorist known for unconventional designs that have influenced contemporary architecture through both practice and theory. He founded the Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA). Notable works: the CCTV Headquarters (Beijing) and the Seattle Central Library.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: World Trade Center (2013), New York City; and Museum Reinhard Ernst (2023), Wiesbaden, Germany. Who is this architect?
n: Fumihiko Maki's notable works are the World Trade Center (2013), a minimalist skyscraper in New York City with a reflective glass facade, and the Museum Reinhard Ernst (2023) in Wiesbaden, Germany, showcasing his signature clean lines and harmonious proportions.

q: Which Spanish architect and engineer, known for sculptural, dynamic structures inspired by natural forms and human anatomy, designed the City of Arts and Sciences in Valencia and the twisting Turning Torso skyscraper in Malmö?
n: A Spanish architect and engineer known for sculptural, dynamic structures often inspired by natural forms and human anatomy. Notable works: the City of Arts and Sciences (Valencia) and the Turning Torso (Malmö), a twisting residential skyscraper.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Einstein Tower in Potsdam, Germany; and the Mossehaus in Berlin. Who is this architect?
n: Erich Mendelsohn's notable works are the Einstein Tower in Potsdam, Germany, and the Mossehaus in Berlin, noted for their dynamic forms and innovative use of materials.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: St. Paul's Cathedral, London; Royal Observatory, Greenwich; and numerous churches in London, including St. Mary-le-Bow and St. Bride's Church. Who is this architect?
n: Sir Christopher Wren's notable works are St. Paul's Cathedral in London, a masterpiece with a prominent dome, the Royal Observatory in Greenwich, and numerous churches in London, including St. Mary-le-Bow and St. Bride's Church.

q: Which English architect, astronomer, and mathematician was instrumental in rebuilding London after the Great Fire of 1666, designing St. Paul's Cathedral and numerous London churches in a style blending classical architecture with Baroque elements?
n: An English architect, astronomer, and mathematician, instrumental in rebuilding London after the Great Fire of 1666. His works are characterized by classical architecture infused with Baroque elements. Notable works: St. Paul's Cathedral and numerous London churches, including St. Mary-le-Bow and St. Bride's.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Flatiron Building in New York City; and the Plan of Chicago (1909). Who is this architect?
n: Daniel Burnham's notable works are the Flatiron Building in New York City and the Plan of Chicago (1909), which laid the foundation for modern urban planning in the U.S.

q: Which Brazilian architect, nicknamed 'the poet of concrete' and 'the great king of curves' for his curvaceous, monumental modernist buildings integral to the identity of Brasília, designed the Cathedral of Brasília and the National Congress of Brazil?
n: A Brazilian architect celebrated for modernist buildings with curvaceous, monumental forms integral to the identity of Brasília, Brazil's capital; nicknamed 'the great king of curves' and 'the poet of concrete.' Notable works: the Cathedral of Brasília, the National Congress of Brazil, and the Palácio da Alvorada.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Munich Olympic Stadium (1972). Who is this architect?
n: Frei Otto's notable work is the Munich Olympic Stadium (1972), known for its sweeping canopies of acrylic glass stabilized by steel cables, mimicking the Alps' silhouettes.

q: What is Kenzo Tange's architectural style?
n: Kenzo Tange's architectural style is Metabolism / Modernism. Kenzo Tange fused traditional Japanese styles with Modernism and influenced the Metabolist movement.

q: Which French structural engineer, celebrated as 'the father of prestressed concrete,' designed the Plougastel Bridge (once the largest reinforced-concrete bridge, with three 187-meter spans) and pioneered thin-shell concrete airship hangars?
n: A pioneering French structural engineer, celebrated as 'the father of prestressed concrete.' His innovations revolutionized the use of concrete, allowing for longer spans and more daring forms. Notable works: the Plougastel Bridge (1930) and the thin-shell concrete Airship Hangars (1923).

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: World Trade Center Twin Towers, New York City; Rainier Tower, Seattle; and Lambert-St. Louis International Airport Terminal, Missouri. Who is this architect?
n: Minoru Yamasaki's notable works are the World Trade Center Twin Towers in New York City, Rainier Tower in Seattle, and the Lambert-St. Louis International Airport Terminal in Missouri.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Säynätsalo Town Hall; Paimio Sanatorium; and Villa Mairea in Finland. Who is this architect?
n: Alvar Aalto's notable works are Säynätsalo Town Hall, Paimio Sanatorium, and Villa Mairea in Finland — exemplary of his holistic design philosophy.

q: What is Moshe Safdie's architectural style?
n: Moshe Safdie's architectural style is Modernism (Humanistic Architecture). Moshe Safdie is celebrated for a humanistic approach to Modernism emphasizing community and livability.

q: What is Louis Sullivan's architectural style?
n: Louis Sullivan's architectural style is Chicago School. Louis Sullivan, the 'Father of Skyscrapers,' was a key figure of the Chicago School.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Whitney Museum of American Art (now the Met Breuer), New York; UNESCO Headquarters, Paris; St. John's Abbey Church, Minnesota; and IBM Research Center, France. Who is this architect?
n: Marcel Breuer's notable works are the Whitney Museum of American Art (now the Met Breuer) in New York, the UNESCO Headquarters in Paris, St. John's Abbey Church in Minnesota, and the IBM Research Center in France.

q: Which French architect and designer, a leading figure of the Art Nouveau movement, created the iconic cast-iron Paris Métro entrances with their sinuous lines and floral motifs?
n: A French architect and designer, a leading figure of the Art Nouveau movement whose curvilinear, ornamental style became synonymous with the movement. Notable work: the cast-iron Paris Métro Entrances (early 1900s), many of which still adorn Paris subway stations today.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Crystal Palace, London. Who is this architect?
n: Joseph Paxton's notable work is the Crystal Palace, London, a pioneering example of prefabricated iron-and-glass architecture built for the Great Exhibition of 1851.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: TWA Flight Center at JFK Airport; Gateway Arch in St. Louis; and Dulles International Airport near Washington, D.C. Who is this architect?
n: Eero Saarinen's notable works are the TWA Flight Center at JFK Airport, the Gateway Arch in St. Louis, and Dulles International Airport near Washington, D.C.

q: Which English gardener, architect, and engineer designed the Crystal Palace for London's Great Exhibition of 1851, a pioneering example of prefabricated iron-and-glass architecture?
n: An English gardener, architect, and engineer, best known for designing the Crystal Palace, a pioneering example of prefabricated iron-and-glass architecture, built for London's Great Exhibition of 1851.

q: Which Belgian architect, a pioneer of the Art Nouveau movement known for integrating architecture with decorative arts and ironwork, designed the Hôtel Tassel in Brussels — considered the first true Art Nouveau building?
n: A Belgian architect and a pioneer of the Art Nouveau movement, noted for the integration of architecture with decorative arts, ironwork, and organic forms. Notable works: the Hôtel Tassel (considered the first true Art Nouveau building), the Hôtel Solvay, and the Horta Museum, Brussels.

q: What is Minoru Yamasaki's architectural style?
n: Minoru Yamasaki's architectural style is Modernism (New Formalism). Minoru Yamasaki's elegant modernist designs are associated with the New Formalism strand of Modernism.

q: What is Michael Graves's architectural style?
n: Michael Graves's architectural style is Postmodernism. Michael Graves was a prominent figure of the Postmodernist movement, blending classical elements with whimsy.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Centre Georges Pompidou, Paris; The Shard, London; and Whitney Museum of American Art, New York. Who is this architect?
n: Renzo Piano's notable works are the Centre Georges Pompidou in Paris, known for its exposed structural elements, The Shard in London, and the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York.

q: Which American architect of Japanese descent, known for elegant modernist designs incorporating elements of serenity and harmony, designed the original World Trade Center Twin Towers?
n: An American architect of Japanese descent, known for elegant, modernist designs that often incorporated elements of serenity and harmony. Notable work: the original World Trade Center Twin Towers, New York City, once the tallest buildings in the world.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Vitra Fire Station, Weil am Rhein, Germany; MAXXI Museum, Rome, Italy; Heydar Aliyev Center, Baku, Azerbaijan; and Guangzhou Opera House, Guangzhou, China. Who is this architect?
n: Zaha Hadid's notable works are the Vitra Fire Station in Weil am Rhein, Germany, the MAXXI Museum in Rome, Italy, the Heydar Aliyev Center in Baku, Azerbaijan — perhaps her most iconic work, a study in seamlessness — and the Guangzhou Opera House in Guangzhou, China.

q: What is Erich Mendelsohn's architectural style?
n: Erich Mendelsohn's architectural style is Expressionism (later International Style). Erich Mendelsohn pioneered Expressionist architecture, later contributing to the International Style.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Turning Torso, Malmö; City of Arts and Sciences, Valencia; and World Trade Center Transportation Hub (Oculus), New York. Who is this architect?
n: Santiago Calatrava's notable works are Turning Torso, a twisting skyscraper in Malmö, the City of Arts and Sciences in Valencia, and the World Trade Center Transportation Hub (Oculus) in New York, a transit station with a winged roof structure.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architectural firm: Willis Tower (formerly Sears Tower), Chicago; Burj Khalifa, Dubai; One World Trade Center, New York; and the Lever House. Which firm is this?
n: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM)'s notable works are the Willis Tower (formerly Sears Tower) in Chicago, once the world's tallest building, the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, the tallest structure globally, One World Trade Center in New York, and the Lever House, pushed toward a new level of architectural recognition by Gordon Bunshaft in 1952.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Pirelli Tower, Milan; Palazzetto dello Sport, Rome; and UNESCO Headquarters, Paris (with Marcel Breuer and Bernard Zehrfuss). Who is this architect?
n: Pier Luigi Nervi's notable works are the Pirelli Tower in Milan, the Palazzetto dello Sport in Rome, and the UNESCO Headquarters in Paris, collaboratively designed with Marcel Breuer and Bernard Zehrfuss.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Habitat '67, Montreal; Jewel Changi Airport, Singapore; and Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, Arkansas. Who is this architect?
n: Moshe Safdie's notable works are Habitat '67 in Montreal, a revolutionary housing complex that reimagined urban living, Jewel Changi Airport in Singapore, and the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art in Arkansas.

q: What is Daniel Burnham's architectural style?
n: Daniel Burnham's architectural style is City Beautiful Movement (Beaux-Arts). Daniel Burnham led the City Beautiful movement, promoting monumental, Beaux-Arts-inspired civic grandeur.

q: Which German-American modernist architect, famous for the aphorism 'Less is more,' designed the Barcelona Pavilion, the Farnsworth House, and the Seagram Building?
n: A German-American modernist architect and pioneer of minimalist architecture, known for his aphorism 'Less is more.' Notable works: the Barcelona Pavilion, the Farnsworth House, the Seagram Building, and Crown Hall at the Illinois Institute of Technology.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Glasgow School of Art; Hill House; and The Willow Tearooms in Scotland. Who is this architect?
n: Charles Rennie Mackintosh's notable works are the Glasgow School of Art, Hill House, and The Willow Tearooms in Scotland, showcasing his distinctive design approach.

q: Which German American architect, known for bold high-tech and postmodern designs, created Terminal 1 at Chicago's O'Hare International Airport, noted for its futuristic design and glass-paneled cylindrical atrium?
n: A German American architect known for high-tech and postmodern designs characterized by bold forms and advanced engineering. Notable work: Terminal 1 at O'Hare International Airport (1987), noted for its futuristic design, efficient passenger flow, and distinctive glass-paneled cylindrical atrium.

q: What is Eero Saarinen's architectural style?
n: Eero Saarinen's architectural style is Modernism (Structural Expressionism). Eero Saarinen's sculptural, curving forms exemplify a Structural Expressionist strand of Modernism.

q: Which American architect, champion of 'organic architecture' who designed more than 1,000 structures over a 70-year career, developed the Prairie House concept of flowing, non-enclosed interior space, and designed Fallingwater, the Robie House, and the spiral-form Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum?
n: An iconic American architect who championed 'organic architecture,' aiming to create structures in harmony with humanity and the environment. He developed the Prairie House concept of open, interpenetrating interior space. Notable works: Fallingwater, the Robie House, Taliesin West, and the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum in New York.

q: Which Israeli Canadian-American architect, celebrated for a humanistic approach emphasizing community and livability, designed the modular housing complex Habitat '67 in Montreal and the waterfall-topped Marina Bay Sands in Singapore?
n: An Israeli Canadian-American architect celebrated for a humanistic approach to architecture that emphasizes community and livability. Notable works: Habitat '67, Montreal — a revolutionary housing complex that reimagined urban living — and Marina Bay Sands, Singapore.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Sydney Opera House, Australia. Who is this architect?
n: Jørn Utzon's notable work is the Sydney Opera House, Australia, celebrated for its innovative use of sculptural forms and integration with the surrounding environment.

q: Which Finnish American architect (father of Eero Saarinen) is recognized for his contributions to Art Nouveau architecture and his later influence on modernist design in the United States, notably at the Cranbrook Educational Community in Michigan?
n: A Finnish American architect recognized for his contributions to Art Nouveau architecture and, later, his influence on modernist design in the United States. Notable work: the Cranbrook Educational Community in Michigan, USA.

q: The following are the notable works of a certain architect: Bauhaus Building, Dessau; Harvard Graduate Center, USA; and Gropius House, Massachusetts. Who is this architect?
n: Walter Gropius's notable works are the Bauhaus Building in Dessau, an embodiment of Bauhaus principles, the Harvard Graduate Center in the USA, which introduced modernist architecture to the campus, and the Gropius House in Massachusetts, his family residence showcasing Bauhaus ideals.

q: What is Helmut Jahn's architectural style?
n: Helmut Jahn's architectural style is High-tech Architecture / Postmodernism. Helmut Jahn blended high-tech and postmodern design with bold forms and advanced engineering.
